# muse — Component Specification **Stage:** Design · **Output:** `spec@1` · **Version:** 1.2.0 Turns UI or design intent into a component spec a developer can implement — including its accessibility behavior — without a single clarifying question. Muse audits the spec, not the implementation. It also has a light, non-binding path for early work: see options first, decide, then carry the choice forward. - **Drafts** a component spec from a requirement or free-text design intent: props, variants, every interactive state, and accessibility criteria as testable propositions - **Audits** the draft, on request, for missing states, missing accessibility criteria, and unmarked invalid prop combinations - **Gates** the spec with a binding, default-fail exit gate before it proceeds to planning - **Sketches** structurally different options, rendered and shown before they are described, with a decision log — no gate, no spec, no tests - **Promotes** a chosen option into a `requirement@1`, the only route from a sketch into the gated stages The `component` skill is one draft-then-gate pipeline with an optional audit, reused unchanged regardless of which component is being specified. `sketch` and `promote` are the exploration path and never gate anything (see `shared/references/architecture/modes.md`). --- ## When to Use - You have a `requirement@1` (or a design description/mockup) and need a formal component spec - You want to check a drafted component spec for missing interactive states or ARIA criteria before it's implemented - You need a binding pass/fail gate on a component spec before it enters planning - You are about to write a component spec by hand: invoke `muse/component` first - You want to see a few directions for a screen or component before deciding what to build (`sketch`), or a chosen option is ready to become real work (`promote`) **Invoke with:** `"Spec this component"`, `"Draft a component spec for this design"`, `"Audit this component spec"`, `"Is this component spec ready?"`, `"Gate this component spec"`, `"Show me some options for this screen"`, `"Promote option B"` Muse specs the component, not the code that implements it. Code-level accessibility scanning of the built component is not yet covered: **[ranger](../ranger/)** has no accessibility hazard pack. --- ## Install **Claude Code** — add the marketplace once, then install by ID: ``` /plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins /plugin install muse ``` **AGY** — installs the full repo; see the [root README](../../README.md#install) for instructions. **Codex** — see the [root Codex setup](../../README.md#codex), then run `codex plugin add muse@wisp-plugins`. --- ## Skills | Skill | What it does | Subagent | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `muse/component` | Drafts, audits, and gates a component `spec@1` — props, variants, per-state behavior, and accessibility criteria as testable propositions | `drafter`, `auditor`, `exit-gate` | | `muse/sketch` | Builds and renders three structurally different options per round, shows them before describing them, and keeps a decision log in an `option-set@1`. Non-binding: no gate, no spec, no tests | `explorer` | | `muse/promote` | Turns a chosen option (or a spike that worked) into a `requirement@1` that carries the decision, the approved render, and what was and was not verified | none | `component` is one skill, not three — the request itself determines which stage runs; there is no separate `muse/draft` or `muse/audit` to invoke. --- ## Subagents | Subagent | Role | Tier | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `drafter` | Component Specification Drafter | sonnet / medium | Produces a `spec@1` from a `requirement@1` or design intent: props, variants, per-state observable behavior, and accessibility criteria. States unknowns in `scope` as assumptions or open owner decisions. Also runs in correction mode. | | `auditor` | Component Specification Auditor | sonnet / medium | On request, adversarially reviews the draft for missing interactive states, missing accessibility criteria, and invalid prop combinations not marked as error cases. | | `exit-gate` | Component Specification Exit Gate | opus / high | Binding pass/fail verdict before the spec enters planning. Default disposition: fail. Two rounds, then escalation to a human. | | `explorer` | Divergent Option Explorer | sonnet / medium | Builds and renders one structurally different option for a sketch and returns an `option-set@1` holding only that option. Writes only to a scratch directory, never ranks options. Internal to `sketch`. | --- ## Pipeline ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; Req["Design intent
requirement@1 or free text"] --> Draft["Drafter
component spec"] Draft --> Gate{{"Exit gate
binding verdict"}} Draft -.->|"on request"| Audit["Auditor
design review"] Audit -.-> Gate Gate -->|"pass"| Spec(["spec@1"]) Gate -.->|"targeted blockers"| Draft class Req source class Draft,Audit engine class Gate router class Spec output ``` # Changelog — muse ## [1.2.0] - 2026-11-14 ### Changed - A direct call to one of this plugin's agents is redirected once per session to the skill that starts it, so that skill's checks run; a second call goes through (`shared/hooks/route-guard.py`, off with `WISP_ROUTE_GUARD=off`). - The exit gate gets two rounds; after a second failing round, or a repeated blocker, the decision goes to you with the persistent blockers (ADR 015). - The drafter self-checks and the gate judges; the auditor runs only when you ask, because it reviewed the same draft. - The gate checks claims and citations against the code, build or spec they refer to; an issue it cannot tie to a source is a note. - Unknowns no longer fail a component spec. The drafter states each in `scope` as an `Assumption:` or, when it changes scope, behavior other work depends on, or cost, an `Open decision:` that comes to you before the gate. The gate blocks only an unknown that leaves a criterion untestable or a decision you have not made (ADR 016). - Pipeline agents' descriptions now say which skill starts them, so work goes through the skill where its checks run; they are also shorter. - Agent prompts drop the `` persona paragraph, leaving four sections; a paired ablation on three agents found no change in what they catch, in output size or in cost (ADR 017). ## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-10 ### Added - `sketch` and `promote` skills and the `explorer` agent: non-binding exploration with three structurally different options per round, a decision log, and `promote` as the only route into the gated pipeline (ADR 011). New schema `option-set@1`. --- name: promote description: >- Use when a chosen sketch option or a spike that worked should become real work: "promote this option", "let's build option B", "turn the chosen design into a requirement", "that spike worked, make it a feature". Turns an option-set@1 or spike-report@1 into a requirement@1 with the decision, render and what was not verified. The only route from exploration into the gated stages; it does not build, spec or plan. version: 1.0.0 --- # Muse — Promote Skill Turns a decision made while exploring into a requirement the gated pipeline can accept. A sketch or a spike is non-binding and never counts as evidence for a gate; this skill is how its result crosses over. It keeps the reason for the decision, the render the owner approved and the list of what was not verified, so the next stage starts from facts and not from a lost conversation. It runs in the primary agent and has no gate of its own; the requirement is gated by the stage that consumes it. None. This skill runs in the primary agent. Do not delegate it. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/references/architecture/modes.md`, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/schemas/option-set@1.json`, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/schemas/spike-report@1.json`, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/schemas/requirement@1.json` **Consumes**: an `option-set@1` with an option whose `status` is `chosen`, or a `spike-report@1` whose `conclusion` is `works` or `partly` **Produces**: a `requirement@1`, written where the repository keeps requirements (a file, or the issue tracker the project uses), with the sketch or spike recorded in `linked_issues` Follow this shape exactly, because the requirement is checked against `requirement@1`: `id` (for example `REQ-001`), `statement`, `stakeholder`, `why`, `done_when` (at least one item), and optionally `out_of_scope`, `priority` (`critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`), `linked_issues` and `reasoning`. No other fields are allowed, so the sketch reference, approved render and verified lists go in `linked_issues` and `done_when`, not in new fields. 1. **Check there is something to promote.** A sketch needs a chosen option; if none is chosen, ask the user to choose or offer another round. A spike with `fails` or `inconclusive` is not promoted; report what it showed and what would answer the question. Do not promote on your own preference. 2. **Draft the `requirement@1`.** - `statement`: what to build, in one sentence, from the chosen option's summary. - `stakeholder`: the brief's audience. - `why`: the brief's problem and the reason recorded for the decision. - `done_when`: conditions a person can check from outside, derived from the chosen option's structure and render, for example "At 390px the navigation opens as a full-height sheet". Include one criterion that the built result matches the approved render at its recorded location in layout and hierarchy, reviewed by the owner. Mark any condition that rests on an unverified assumption, and carry the unverified items forward as conditions to confirm. - `out_of_scope`: the brief's non-goals, plus each rejected and parked option by name with its reason. - `linked_issues`: the sketch or spike and option (for example `SKETCH-001/OPT-rail`), the path of the artifact, and the approved render. 3. **Keep the log honest.** Make sure the sketch is `decided` and its `decisions` include the choice; for a spike, copy its `verified` and `unverified` lists. Do not rewrite earlier entries.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Warn when a decision record reads like a session log or holds more than one decision.

Usage: python3 scripts/check-adr-style.py [directory]   (default docs/adr)

A record lets a reader two years on see what was decided, why, what was rejected, what it costs and when to
revisit it, with a pointer to the evidence. Measurements, run counts, one-off test dates and a tour of the
investigation belong in the evaluation log, the commit or the pull request. The check only warns: judgment
stays with the writer, and a long record that earns its length can say so in review. See
shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

WORD_REVIEW = 600
MARKERS = (
    (re.compile(r"\blive runs?\b", re.I), "a live run is evidence for the log, not the record"),
    (re.compile(r"\b(?:in|during) this session\b", re.I), "session narration"),
    (re.compile(r"\b\d[\d,]*\s+(?:runs?|calls?|rounds?|sessions?|transcripts?|findings|tokens)\b", re.I), "a count from one investigation"),
    (re.compile(r"\bone run (?:each|per)\b", re.I), "a run count"),
    (re.compile(r"\b(?:on|since|as of)\s+20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d\b", re.I), "a one-off date"),
    (re.compile(r"\bnot yet (?:measured|verified|tested)\b", re.I), "an open-measurement list; keep one `Revisit when` instead"),
)


def body(text: str) -> str:
    """The record without its title, Status and Date lines, which legitimately carry dates and links."""
    lines = [line for line in text.splitlines() if not line.startswith(("# ", "**Status:**", "**Date:**", "**Amends:**", "**Supersedes:**"))]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def review(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    notes = []
    words = len(body(text).split())
    if words > WORD_REVIEW:
        notes.append(f"{words} words: a record this long often holds several decisions (split it) or a session log (move the log)")
    for pattern, reason in MARKERS:
        hits = pattern.findall(body(text))
        if hits:
            notes.append(f"transient detail ({reason}): {hits[0]!r}")
    return notes


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    directory = Path(argv[1]) if len(argv) > 1 else Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "docs" / "adr"
    records = sorted(path for path in directory.glob("[0-9][0-9][0-9]-*.md"))
    flagged = 0
    for path in records:
        notes = review(path)
        if notes:
            flagged += 1
            print(f"WARN: {path.name}")
            for note in notes:
                print(f"    {note}")
    if flagged:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Warn when a decision record reads like a session log or holds more than one decision.

Usage: python3 scripts/check-adr-style.py [directory]   (default docs/adr)

A record lets a reader two years on see what was decided, why, what was rejected, what it costs and when to
revisit it, with a pointer to the evidence. Measurements, run counts, one-off test dates and a tour of the
investigation belong in the evaluation log, the commit or the pull request. The check only warns: judgment
stays with the writer, and a long record that earns its length can say so in review. See
shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

WORD_REVIEW = 600
MARKERS = (
    (re.compile(r"\blive runs?\b", re.I), "a live run is evidence for the log, not the record"),
    (re.compile(r"\b(?:in|during) this session\b", re.I), "session narration"),
    (re.compile(r"\b\d[\d,]*\s+(?:runs?|calls?|rounds?|sessions?|transcripts?|findings|tokens)\b", re.I), "a count from one investigation"),
    (re.compile(r"\bone run (?:each|per)\b", re.I), "a run count"),
    (re.compile(r"\b(?:on|since|as of)\s+20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d\b", re.I), "a one-off date"),
    (re.compile(r"\bnot yet (?:measured|verified|tested)\b", re.I), "an open-measurement list; keep one `Revisit when` instead"),
)


def body(text: str) -> str:
    """The record without its title, Status and Date lines, which legitimately carry dates and links."""
    lines = [line for line in text.splitlines() if not line.startswith(("# ", "**Status:**", "**Date:**", "**Amends:**", "**Supersedes:**"))]
    return "\n".join(lines)

    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    notes = []
    words = len(body(text).split())
    if words > WORD_REVIEW:
        notes.append(f"{words} words: a record this long often holds several decisions (split it) or a session log (move the log)")
    for pattern, reason in MARKERS:
        hits = pattern.findall(body(text))
        if hits:
            notes.append(f"transient detail ({reason}): {hits[0]!r}")
    return notes

    for path in records:
        notes = review(path)
        if notes:
            flagged += 1
            print(f"WARN: {path.name}")
            for note in notes:

    return 0

# Cross-Harness Authoring

Use this guide when a change affects Claude/AGY source plugins, Codex-native plugins, shared artifact contracts, or generated Codex distribution.

## Design boundary

Shared sources preserve lifecycle identity and interoperable artifacts. Harness sources preserve execution quality. Never mechanically translate prompts, model tiers, named agents, or delegation topology across harnesses.

| Concern | Shared source | Claude/AGY source | Codex source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Identity | ID, version, author, `consumes`, `produces` | Uses `plugins/<id>/plugin.json` | Native manifest matches ID, version, and author |
| Artifact contract | Versioned JSON schema | Produces and consumes the schema | Produces and consumes the same schema bytes |
| Skill inventory | Lifecycle route name | `plugins/<id>/skills/<skill>/` | Same route name under `harnesses/codex/plugins/<id>/skills/` |
| Workflow | None | Specialist agents and Claude-native orchestration | Native skill plus optional Codex role cards |
| Delegation | None | Named source agents | `agent-roles/<role>.md` selected only for bounded independent work |

Codex role cards are portable plugin resources. They are not TOML configuration: host TOML controls local runtime defaults and is never a marketplace contract.

Codex's own custom agents are TOML files (`.codex/agents/<name>.toml` with `name`, `description` and `developer_instructions`, and optionally a model and reasoning effort). A subagent inherits the parent's sandbox and approvals, and an agent file cannot override them, so a role card cannot make a role read-only by itself: the skill states the write boundary in its delegation packet and the primary agent checks the result. Codex also starts subagents only when the skill or the user asks, so a delegating skill must say which role to start and with what packet; "when teams are available" never triggers delegation. Whether to offer an optional, non-contract generator that turns role cards into TOML for users who want named Codex agents is an open decision (proposed decision record N8).

## Claude-only enforcement

Two Claude Code hooks enforce rules the skill text also states: the handback validator (`shared/hooks/validate-handback.py`) checks each exit gate's `verdict@3` and the retry cap (ADR 012, ADR 015), and the routing guard (`shared/hooks/route-guard.py`) sends a direct call to a pipeline agent through its skill first. Codex and Antigravity have neither, so a Codex skill must carry the rule itself (gate rounds, escalation, behavior evidence) and cannot rely on a hook to catch a miss.

## Change procedure

1. Classify the change before editing: shared identity, shared artifact contract, Claude/AGY workflow, Codex workflow, or distribution only.
2. Read the counterpart source before deciding whether it needs a change. Preserve lifecycle intent and artifact validity; do not preserve wording or topology by default.
3. For an identity or schema change, update the shared source first. Version an incompatible schema, update every affected producer and consumer, then update both harness workflows.
4. For a new or renamed lifecycle skill, add the route to both harnesses. Match the directory name, not the prompt body. Author the Codex skill independently for its tools, context model, and delegation behavior.
5. For a Claude agent change, decide explicitly whether Codex needs a skill workflow or role-card change. A Claude prompt is not input to a Codex role card.
6. For a Codex role-card change, update every delegating skill whose task boundary or required evidence changes. Each delegation must carry the `agent-roles/README.md` packet. Keep the primary agent responsible for synthesis, judgment, and external writes.
7. For a Codex-only UI, model, category, or description change, do not alter the Claude prompt unless lifecycle intent changed.

## Required change record

Record this in the pull request description, implementation report, or task handoff whenever a cross-harness source changes:

```text
Classification: <shared contract | Claude/AGY workflow | Codex workflow | distribution>
Counterpart reviewed: <paths>
Intent preserved: <artifact, evidence, acceptance criteria, or lifecycle rule>
Intentional divergence: <why the harness differs, or none>
Codex role impact: <role cards and skills changed, or none>
Verification: <commands and behavioral checks>
```

## Runtime reference packaging

An exact `shared/schemas/...` or `shared/references/...` path in Codex runtime guidance declares a load dependency. Add it to the plugin's `runtime_files`; the bundle builder materializes it as a regular file.

The reference-closure check follows exact paths transitively through loaded reference files. Historical prose should name an artifact without its repository path unless the running skill must open that file.

## Review questions

- Does a consumer still receive a valid versioned artifact from either harness?
- Does the Codex skill have a complete single-agent path when multi-agent work is unavailable?
- If it delegates, are role, input boundary, write authority, and output evidence explicit?
- Does the delegation packet make owned paths, exclusions, evidence, and completion unambiguous?
- Did the change preserve an outcome or merely copy a source prompt's incidental wording?
- Does the generated bundle contain the exact native sources and only the runtime resources that skill needs?

## Deliberate non-goals

- No prompt generator transforms Claude agents into Codex roles.
- No TOML agent file is shipped as a plugin behavior contract.
- No behavioral equivalence claim is made from directory or schema parity alone; use a representative artifact and evidence review when changing a critical route.

{
  "name": "guide",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Start work by intent (explore, spike, fix, build, check, ship) and hand off to the skill that does it, so its checks run.",
  "author": {
    "name": "Gabriel Castro",
    "email": "gabe@techworx.dev"
  },
  "skills": "./skills/",
  "interface": {
    "displayName": "Guide",
    "shortDescription": "Start work by intent; route to the right skill.",
    "longDescription": "Six intent commands that pick a path by risk and hand off to the Wisp skill that does the work, so its verification runs.",
    "developerName": "Gabriel Castro",
    "category": "plan",
    "capabilities": [
      "skills"
    ],
    "defaultPrompt": [
      "Fix this bug through the fix path, with a test that fails on the original bug."
    ]
  }
}
---
name: fix
description: Fix a bug or a list of review findings with a test that fails on the original bug. Use for "fix this" or "address these findings".
---

# Guide: fix

Say "Mode: fix." Use `smith:implement` with a fix brief: the claim to fix, the invariants that must hold, and where the same mistake may repeat. A one- or two-line fix with an obvious cause can be done directly with a test that fails on the original bug; say the full path was skipped and why.
---
name: gate
description: Independently verify an artifact against its criteria before it crosses a lifecycle boundary. Use this, not freehand checking, for “is this done?”, “verify this”, and readiness checks on requirements, specs, plans, implementations, and PRs.
---

State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.

# Gate a lifecycle artifact with evidence

Sentinel judges an existing artifact; it does not author a replacement. Begin by identifying what the artifact claims, where it is persisted, and which criteria actually govern it.

## Workflow

1. Identify `artifact_type`, `artifact_path`, the authoritative criteria, linked artifacts, and source files that can prove or disprove each criterion.
2. Read persisted files when a path is present rather than relying on conversation summaries.
3. Build an evidence table that classifies each criterion as verified, failed, or unverifiable, with exact paths and test or inspection evidence.
4. Produce `verdict@3` conforming to `shared/schemas/verdict@3.json`. Name the verified scope, blockers, coverage gaps, and pending checks.
5. Pass only when every applicable criterion is verified. On failure, return specific blockers that the producing workflow can act on.

## Retry protocol

Round one lists the complete blocker set. On a retry (`retry_count` 1 or more, with the previous blockers supplied), inspect only the revised artifact and cite only unresolved prior blockers or regressions the fix introduced; record other new issues as non-blocking coverage gaps. A fail on the retry, or a blocker repeating unchanged, returns an `escalation_required` blocker for a human instead of another round. Check each claim against the code, build or spec it cites.

## Evidence and safety

- Do not treat a passing test alone as proof of a criterion it does not exercise. A criterion about behavior is verified by running changed logic on real inputs (`shared/references/verification/evidence.md`); structural checks are not behavior evidence.
- An outcome criterion (`Outcome: <measure> at least <threshold> against <named baseline>, measured by <method>`) is verified only by a recorded run of the baseline and the product the same way (`shared/references/verification/evidence.md`); without one it is a pending check and the gate does not pass beyond the verified scope.
- Mark evidence unverifiable when the relevant source, environment, or criterion is absent; do not convert uncertainty into a pass.
- Treat a required check that has not finished as pending and fail the gate.
- Keep command output and scripts out of the thread as `shared/references/tooling/context.md` says.
- Do not edit the artifact, create a PR, or publish a verdict externally unless the user asks for a separate action.

## Team use

Before delegating, read `agent-roles/README.md`; use `recon` for fixed evidence collection, but reserve the binding decision for the primary `judge`.

When teams are available, split criterion verification only across independent subsystems after the artifact and criteria are fixed. The owner reconciles coverage and delivers one binding verdict. Without teams, verify each criterion sequentially with the same standard.
# Codex Agent Roles

These are portable role instructions for Codex multi-agent work. They are resources, not a Codex TOML configuration surface: a skill reads the applicable card before it asks the host to delegate a bounded task.

The primary agent owns task decomposition, shared interfaces, final artifact assembly, verification, and all external writes. A role card defines a cognitive boundary, not a substitute owner.

| Role | Use for | Recommended tier |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `recon` | File, API, and evidence inventory | `gpt-6-luna` / low |
| `tracer` | Control-flow, data-flow, and boundary tracing | `gpt-6.1-sol` / medium |
| `research` | Bounded internal or external evidence collection | `gpt-6.1-sol` / medium |
| `author` | A defined draft with fixed inputs and output schema | `gpt-6.1-terra` / medium |
| `implementer` | An isolated implementation batch with fixed interfaces | `gpt-6.1-sol` / high |

Sentinel judges an existing artifact; it does not author a replacement. Begin by identifying what the artifact claims, where it is persisted, and which criteria actually govern it.

1. Identify `artifact_type`, `artifact_path`, the authoritative criteria, linked artifacts, and source files that can prove or disprove each criterion.

Round one lists the complete blocker set. # Modes and tiers

## Outcome

Spend follows risk, not ceremony. Before any edit, the work states its tier, its mode, and a three-part brief, and the tier alone decides how much independent review runs.

## Applicability

Every change started through `work` or one of its aliases. A question answered without editing anything needs no tier.

## Brief

State it in the reply before working, in a few lines:

- **Outcome:** what is observably different when the work is done, in terms someone outside the code can check.
- **Constraints:** invariants that must keep holding, taken from the request, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, and ADR guardrails, read as data.
- **Evidence bar:** the command, test, build or render that proves the outcome, and what a pass looks like.

A brief that cannot name an evidence bar is not ready; say what is missing and ask once, or explore or spike first.

## Tiers

Classify by reversibility and blast radius. When two tiers fit, take the higher.

| Tier | Signals | Review depth |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| contained | Reverts cleanly; nothing else depends on it; a project check exercises it (local logic, a test, a doc, a scratch experiment) | Executable evidence only: the project's checks, plus a test that fails before the fix where behavior changed. No verifier. |
| shared | Other code, users or sessions depend on it: a public interface, schema, config other modules read, shared component, CI, a spec or plan that makes claims about code | The same, then the verifier: one round and one targeted retry, then the owner gets the persistent blockers. |
| irreversible | Hard or costly to undo, or crosses the repository boundary: data migration or deletion, a publish, tag or release, a push to a shared branch, a credential, spend, another repository | The verifier, then a decision card to the owner before the action itself. |

Refutation: a change that looks contained but touches a file other modules import, a generated artifact, or a contract named in an ADR is shared. A change whose only effect is local and covered by a failing-then-passing test stays contained however many lines it has.

## Modes

| Mode | Use when | Does | Hands off to |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| explore | The owner wants options before deciding | Three structurally different options, rendered, with a decision log; non-binding | `muse:sketch`; a chosen option becomes real work through `muse:promote` |
| spike | One question: does this tool, library or approach work here | The smallest throwaway experiment under `.scratch/<id>/`; returns `spike-report@1` with what was observed, verified and not verified; edits no source | `muse:promote` when it works and should become real work |
| fix | Something is broken or a review left findings | A test that fails on the original defect and passes after; search where the same mistake repeats; the project's checks | The verifier at shared tier and above |
| build | A feature or change with a known outcome | Brief, then the work in one context; a spec or plan only when `shared/references/work/specs-and-plans.md` says one pays | The verifier at shared tier and above |
| check | Existing work needs confirming, or code needs a defect hunt | Confirmation: the verifier against the brief or the artifact's criteria. Defect hunt: hazard packs, then the adversary on each suspected defect | Findings go to fix mode |
| ship | The work is ready to go out | Only the steps asked for: `courier:changeset`, then `courier:commit`, `courier:pr`, `courier:release` | The owner confirms before anything is pushed, posted or published |

A spike or sketch is never evidence that production code is correct, has no gate, and enters real work only through `muse:promote` (ADR 011).

## Autonomy by reversibility

| Action | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| Read, measure, run checks, work in a worktree or draft branch, fix a failing check inside the brief, write a proposal or decision card | Do it; report it in the output |
| Tighten a check that encodes an already-decided rule and passes today, open a pull request | Do it and say so; the pull request is the review |
| Change a guardrail or ADR, loosen any check, add or remove an agent or plugin, publish a schema version, tag or release, push to a shared branch, change a model tier, touch another repository | Decision card first |

Tightening a decided check may be unasked; loosening one never is.

## Output at the edge

The owner reads only: the diff or render, the evidence (each command and its observed result), a `Not verified:` list, and the pull request or changelog text. `Not verified:` names every check that did not run, every platform or input not exercised, and every claim resting on another agent's summary; when nothing is left out, say `Not verified: nothing beyond the evidence above`. A reply that took a lighter path than its tier names what it skipped and why.

## Disposition

- Tier and mode stated, evidence bar met, `Not verified:` present: done.
- Evidence bar not met: keep working or report the gap as not verified; never report it done.
- Verifier escalated: stop retrying and give the owner the persistent blockers.

# Decision cards

## Outcome

The owner decides only what changes scope or cannot be undone, in under a minute per decision, and the answer survives the session.

## Applicability

Raise a card when the answer changes scope, behavior other work depends on, or cost the owner carries, or when the next action is irreversible (`shared/references/work/modes.md`, Tiers and Autonomy). Everything else proceeds on a stated assumption: write `Assumption: <the answer the work proceeds on>` in the reply and keep going.

No trigger, no card. A preference question, a naming choice, or a step the repository already answers is not a card.

## Shape

```text
Decision: <the question, one line>
Why now: <the trigger and its evidence: a file, a failing check, a cost>
Options:
  A. <option> — cost, risk, reversibility
  B. <structurally different option> — cost, risk, reversibility
Recommendation: <A or B>, confidence <high | medium | low>, because <reason>
Default if unanswered: <what happens, and when>
Expires: <the point after which the card is withdrawn or the default applies>
```

- **Options differ in structure,** not in a parameter of one idea. If only one real option exists, say so and ask for a yes or no.
- **What would change the answer:** one line, when a fact the owner may know would flip the recommendation.
- **Irreversible actions have no default that acts.** The default for a publish, push, deletion or migration is to wait.

## Limits

- At most three open cards at once; batch them in one message, most consequential first.
- Do not repeat a card the owner already answered; fold the answer in.
- Do not ask before reading what the repository says: `AGENTS.md`, ADR guardrails and existing specs answer many questions.

## Encode the answer

A decision that lives only in a chat or in memory is lost. When the owner answers:

- A rule for every session goes in `AGENTS.md`, or becomes a check (a hook, a test, a lint) when a machine can decide it.
- An architectural choice that passes both gates in `shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md` gets a decision record.
- A scope answer goes in the brief, the spec's `scope`, or the pull request body, wherever the next reader acts on it.

## Refutation

A card is wrong when the repository already decides the question, when the answer would not change what is built, or when it hides a recommendation the agent could act on reversibly. Proceed on an assumption instead and list it in the output.

## Disposition

- Answered: encode it and continue.
- Unanswered by expiry: apply the stated default, or keep waiting for an irreversible action, and say which.
- Declined: record the decision as declined with the reason, so it is not raised again without new evidence.

# Decision cards

## Outcome

The owner decides only what changes scope or cannot be undone, in under a minute per decision, and the answer survives the session.

## Applicability

Raise a card when the answer changes scope, behavior other work depends on, or cost the owner carries, or when the next action is irreversible (`shared/references/work/modes.md`, Tiers and Autonomy). Everything else proceeds on a stated assumption: write `Assumption: <the answer the work proceeds on>` in the reply and keep going.

No trigger, no card. A preference question, a naming choice, or a step the repository already answers is not a card.

## Shape

```text
Decision: <the question, one line>
Why now: <the trigger and its evidence: a file, a failing check, a cost>
Options:
  A. <option> — cost, risk, reversibility
  B. <structurally different option> — cost, risk, reversibility
Recommendation: <A or B>, confidence <high | medium | low>, because <reason>
Default if unanswered: <what happens, and when>
Expires: <the point after which the card is withdrawn or the default applies>
```

- **Options differ in structure,** not in a parameter of one idea. If only one real option exists, say so and ask for a yes or no.
- **What would change the answer:** one line, when a fact the owner may know would flip the recommendation.
- **Irreversible actions have no default that acts.** The default for a publish, push, deletion or migration is to wait.

## Limits

- At most three open cards at once; batch them in one message, most consequential first.
- Do not repeat a card the owner already answered; fold the answer in.
- Do not ask before reading what the repository says: `AGENTS.md`, ADR guardrails and existing specs answer many questions.

## Encode the answer

A decision that lives only in a chat or in memory is lost. When the owner answers:

- A rule for every session goes in `AGENTS.md`, or becomes a check (a hook, a test, a lint) when a machine can decide it.
- An architectural choice that passes both gates in `shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md` gets a decision record.
- A scope answer goes in the brief, the spec's `scope`, or the pull request body, wherever the next reader acts on it.

A card is wrong when the repository already decides the question, when the answer would not change what is built, or when it hides a recommendation the agent could act on reversibly. Proceed on an assumption instead and list it in the output.

- Answered: encode it and continue.
- Unanswered by expiry: apply the stated default, or keep waiting for an irreversible action, and say which.

# Verifier brief

## Outcome

An independent check whose independence is real: the verifier sees what the work claims and what changed, never how the worker reasoned, and tests each claim by running something.

## Applicability

The verifier runs for shared and irreversible work, and for a spec or plan that makes claims about code (`shared/references/work/modes.md`). It does not run for contained work with executable evidence; the project's checks and the stop hook cover that tier.

## What the caller passes

| Field | Content |
| :-- | :-- |
| Brief | Outcome, constraints and evidence bar, as stated before the work began |
| Tier | `shared` or `irreversible`, and why |
| Change | The diff range or base revision (`<base>..HEAD`, or the uncommitted tree), or the artifact path for a spec or plan |
| Evidence | Each claim the work makes, with the command run and the observed result |
| Not verified | The worker's own list |
| Round | `retry_count` (0 on the first round) and, on a retry, only the prior round's `blockers` |

## What the caller withholds

- The worker's reasoning, plan, scratch notes, transcript or conversation summary.
- Arguments for why a claim holds. A claim and its evidence are enough; persuasion is what fresh context exists to resist.
- Unrelated files or history. The verifier reads the repository itself.

## A brief the verifier can check

- Each outcome is observable: a command's output, a page state, a returned value, a file's contents.
- Each constraint names where it can break: a caller, a contract, a config reader.
- The evidence bar names a command or render, not "tests pass".

A brief that fails these is returned as a fail with a blocker on criterion `brief`. A vague brief brings back the old failure: padding, wording churn, and blockers that cannot be acted on.

## What the verifier does with it

- Treats the brief's outcomes and constraints as the criteria and the evidence list as leads, not proof.
- Runs the changed code on representative and edge inputs from the brief, the build, or a render, per `shared/references/verification/evidence.md`.
- Searches for the same mistake where it is likely to repeat: callers, siblings with the same responsibility, generated copies.
- Returns `verdict@3` with blockers that cite evidence and state the change required.

## Rounds

- Round one lists the complete blocker set.
- The worker fixes only those blockers, then resubmits with `retry_count` 1 and the prior blockers.
- A fail on the second round, or a blocker repeated unchanged, carries an `escalation_required` blocker. The caller stops and gives the owner the persistent blockers; there is no third round.
- An outcome claimed against a baseline ("faster than", "replaces", "matches") stays pending until a result shows both run the same way.

## Disputed findings

When the worker believes a blocker is wrong, or acting on a finding is costly, send that one finding to the adversary instead of arguing in a retry. A `dismissed` assessment with code evidence goes back to the verifier as evidence; `confirmed` or `plausible` stays a blocker or goes to the owner.

## Refutation

The check was not independent if the verifier received the worker's reasoning, if it passed on evidence it did not run or read, or if it ran in the worker's own context. Record any of these in the output's `Not verified:` list.

## Disposition

- Pass: report the verified scope; non-blocking gaps go in the `Not verified:` list.
- Fail, round one: fix the blockers and retry once.
- Escalated: stop; owner decides with the persistent blockers.

# When a spec or plan is worth writing

## Outcome

A spec or plan exists only where a reader needs it: the owner wants to read the contract before code exists, or other work will be built against it. It is never a mandatory stage.

## Applicability

Build mode, before the work starts. Fix, spike and explore never need one.

## Write a spec when

- **Shared contract:** other code, teams or sessions will be built against the behavior (a public API, a schema, a shared component, a protocol).
- **The owner asks to read it** before code exists, or the brief has open decisions that a written contract would settle faster than a render.
- **A UI component** whose states and accessibility must not regress: use `muse:component`, which drafts and gates a `spec@1`.

A spec follows `shared/schemas/spec@1.json` and the checklist and unknowns rules in `shared/references/verification/gate-readiness.md`: falsifiable criteria, error cases marked, unknowns stated as `Assumption:` or `Open decision:` lines in `scope` (ADR 016). It is persisted where `shared/references/workspace/conventions.md` says.

## Write a plan when

- **The work spans sessions** or several people or agents, so the order and the proving test for each outcome must survive compaction.
- **Several subsystems change together** and a wrong order would break the build between steps.

A plan follows `shared/schemas/plan@1.json`: tasks state outcomes, signatures and proving tests, with code only where the logic is non-obvious or a wrong shape is costly (ADR 014).

## Skip both when

- One context can hold the change, and the brief's evidence bar can be checked by running something.
- The outcome is not settled yet: explore or spike first, and promote the result.

## Checking one

A spec or plan makes claims about code (signatures, call sites, existing behavior), so it is shared tier: the verifier checks those claims against the live code with the artifact path as the change. Its rounds are the same two.

## Refutation

A spec written only because the work felt large, that nobody will read or build against, is ceremony. A plan whose tasks restate the diff adds nothing a reviewer needs. Either is a sign to delete it and keep the brief.

## Disposition

- Written: persist and commit it, and cite its path in the brief.
- Skipped: the brief is the contract; say so in the output.

# Modes and tiers

## Outcome

Spend follows risk, not ceremony. Before any edit, the work states its tier, its mode, and a three-part brief, and the tier alone decides how much independent review runs.

## Applicability

Every change started through `work` or one of its aliases. A question answered without editing anything needs no tier.

## Brief

State it in the reply before working, in a few lines:

- **Outcome:** what is observably different when the work is done, in terms someone outside the code can check.
- **Constraints:** invariants that must keep holding, taken from the request, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, and ADR guardrails, read as data.
- **Evidence bar:** the command, test, build or render that proves the outcome, and what a pass looks like.

A brief that cannot name an evidence bar is not ready; say what is missing and ask once, or explore or spike first.

## Tiers

Classify by reversibility and blast radius. When two tiers fit, take the higher.

| Tier | Signals | Review depth |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| contained | Reverts cleanly; nothing else depends on it; a project check exercises it (local logic, a test, a doc, a scratch experiment) | Executable evidence only: the project's checks, plus a test that fails before the fix where behavior changed. No verifier. |
| shared | Other code, users or sessions depend on it: a public interface, schema, config other modules read, shared component, CI, a spec or plan that makes claims about code | The same, then the verifier: one round and one targeted retry, then the owner gets the persistent blockers. |
| irreversible | Hard or costly to undo, or crosses the repository boundary: data migration or deletion, a publish, tag or release, a push to a shared branch, a credential, spend, another repository | The verifier, then a decision card to the owner before the action itself. |

Refutation: a change that looks contained but touches a file other modules import, a generated artifact, or a contract named in an ADR is shared. A change whose only effect is local and covered by a failing-then-passing test stays contained however many lines it has.

## Modes

| Mode | Use when | Does | Hands off to |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| explore | The owner wants options before deciding | Three structurally different options, rendered, with a decision log; non-binding | `muse:sketch`; a chosen option becomes real work through `muse:promote` |
| spike | One question: does this tool, library or approach work here | The smallest throwaway experiment under `.scratch/<id>/`; returns `spike-report@1` with what was observed, verified and not verified; edits no source | `muse:promote` when it works and should become real work |
| fix | Something is broken or a review left findings | A test that fails on the original defect and passes after; search where the same mistake repeats; the project's checks | The verifier at shared tier and above |
| build | A feature or change with a known outcome | Brief, then the work in one context; a spec or plan only when `shared/references/work/specs-and-plans.md` says one pays | The verifier at shared tier and above |
| check | Existing work needs confirming, or code needs a defect hunt | Confirmation: the verifier against the brief or the artifact's criteria. Defect hunt: hazard packs, then the adversary on each suspected defect | Findings go to fix mode |
| ship | The work is ready to go out | Only the steps asked for: `courier:changeset`, then `courier:commit`, `courier:pr`, `courier:release` | The owner confirms before anything is pushed, posted or published |

A spike or sketch is never evidence that production code is correct, has no gate, and enters real work only through `muse:promote` (ADR 011).

## Autonomy by reversibility

| Action | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| Read, measure, run checks, work in a worktree or draft branch, fix a failing check inside the brief, write a proposal or decision card | Do it; report it in the output |
| Tighten a check that encodes an already-decided rule and passes today, open a pull request | Do it and say so; the pull request is the review |
| Change a guardrail or ADR, loosen any check, add or remove an agent or plugin, publish a schema version, tag or release, push to a shared branch, change a model tier, touch another repository | Decision card first |

Tightening a decided check may be unasked; loosening one never is.

## Output at the edge

The owner reads only: the diff or render, the evidence (each command and its observed result), a `Not verified:` list, and the pull request or changelog text. `Not verified:` names every check that did not run, every platform or input not exercised, and every claim resting on another agent's summary; when nothing is left out, say `Not verified: nothing beyond the evidence above`. A reply that took a lighter path than its tier names what it skipped and why.

## Disposition

- Tier and mode stated, evidence bar met, `Not verified:` present: done.
- Evidence bar not met: keep working or report the gap as not verified; never report it done.
- Verifier escalated: stop retrying and give the owner the persistent blockers.

"""Write the six alias skills for plugins/wisp (one-off authoring helper)."""
from pathlib import Path
import sys

ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1])
ALIASES = {
    "explore": (
        'Use when the owner wants to see ideas before deciding: "explore this", "show me options", "what could this look like", "try a few directions". Starts `wisp:work` in explore mode: structurally different options, rendered, with a decision log through `muse:sketch`. Non-binding; nothing is built for real.',
        "explore",
    ),
    "spike": (
        'Use when the question is whether something works before committing to it: "spike this", "does X work in our stack", "try it out", "quick prototype to check". Starts `wisp:work` in spike mode: the smallest throwaway experiment in a scratch directory, returning a spike-report@1 with what was and was not verified.',
        "spike",
    ),
    "fix": (
        'Use when something is broken or a review left findings: "fix this", "this is broken", "address these findings", "make this small change". Starts `wisp:work` in fix mode: a test that fails on the original defect and passes after, a search for the same mistake elsewhere, and the verifier when the fix touches shared code.',
        "fix",
    ),
    "build": (
        'Use when building a feature or a change other work will depend on: "build this", "add this feature", "implement this", "let\'s do this for real". Starts `wisp:work` in build mode: a brief with outcome, constraints and evidence bar, a spec or plan only where one pays, and the verifier for shared or irreversible work.',
        "build",
    ),
    "check": (
        'Use when work needs confirming or code needs a defect hunt: "check this", "is this done", "verify this before we ship", "find bugs in this", "audit this". Starts `wisp:work` in check mode: the fresh-context verifier against the brief or criteria, or hazard packs plus the adversary on each suspected defect.',
        "check",
    ),
    "ship": (
        'Use when work is ready to go out: "ship this", "commit and open a PR", "write the changeset", "cut a release". Starts `wisp:work` in ship mode, which runs only the courier steps asked for (changeset, commit, pull request, release notes) and confirms before anything is pushed, posted or published.',
        "ship",
    ),
}

for name, (description, mode) in ALIASES.items():
    assert len(description) <= 450, (name, len(description))
    path = ROOT / "plugins" / "wisp" / "skills" / name / "SKILL.md"
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(
        f"---\nname: {name}\ndescription: >-\n  {description}\nversion: 1.0.0\n---\n\n"
        f"# Wisp — {name.capitalize()}\n\n"
        f"Start the `wisp:work` skill in {mode} mode with the user's request.\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(name, len(description))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Claude Code Stop hook: ask once for a "Not verified" statement when work is left uncommitted.

Registered by plugins/wisp/hooks/hooks.json:

  {"hooks": {"Stop": [{"hooks": [
    {"type": "command", "command": "python3 \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/hooks/stop-check.py\""}]}]}}

Why: agents report success without saying what they did not check. A prompt asking for the list is
not enforced; a hook is. The owner reads the diff, the evidence and the `Not verified:` list, so a
turn that leaves changes in the tree must end with that list.

Behavior
  - Reads the Stop hook JSON from stdin (`cwd`, `session_id`, `stop_hook_active`,
    `last_assistant_message`, `transcript_path`).
  - Lets the stop through when `stop_hook_active` is set (the agent is already continuing because
    of a stop hook), when `cwd` is not a work tree or the tree is clean, when the final assistant
    message contains "not verified" (any case), or when the tree is unchanged since the last stop
    this hook let through for the session. The last rule keeps a question asked over an
    already-reported dirty tree from being blocked again.
  - Otherwise blocks once with {"decision": "block", "reason": ...}. The agent adds the line and
    stops; the next Stop carries `stop_hook_active` and passes.
  - The final message comes from `last_assistant_message`, or, when that is absent, from the last
    assistant text in the transcript file.

    tree fingerprint is kept (default: the system temp directory).
  - Fails open: any internal error exits 1 with nothing on stdout, which does not block.
  - Standard library only.

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

MARKER = re.compile(r"not\s+verified", re.IGNORECASE)
TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5
REASON = (
    "There are uncommitted changes and your final message has no \"Not verified:\" line. "
    "Before stopping, add one listing what you did not check (checks not run, platforms or inputs "
    "not exercised, claims resting on another agent's summary), or \"Not verified: nothing beyond "
    "the evidence above\"."
)


def tree_status(cwd: str) -> str | None:
    """Porcelain status of the work tree at `cwd`, or None when it is not a work tree."""
    completed = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", cwd, "status", "--porcelain=v1", "-z", "--untracked-files=all"],
        capture_output=True,
        timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
        check=False,
    )
    if completed.returncode != 0:
        return None
    return completed.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")


def fingerprint(cwd: str, status: str) -> str:
    """Hash of the status plus each changed path's size and modification time."""
    digest = hashlib.sha256(status.encode("utf-8"))
    tokens = status.split("\0")
    index = 0
    while index < len(tokens):
        entry = tokens[index]
        index += 1
        if len(entry) < 4:
            continue
        code, path = entry[:2], entry[3:]
        if "R" in code or "C" in code:
            index += 1  # the next token is the original path of a rename or copy
        try:
            stat = (Path(cwd) / path).stat()
            digest.update(f"{path}:{stat.st_size}:{stat.st_mtime_ns}".encode("utf-8"))
        except OSError:

        return ""
    last = ""
    with open(transcript, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for line in handle:
            try:
                record = json.loads(line)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if not isinstance(record, dict) or record.get("type") != "assistant":
                continue
            content = (record.get("message") or {}).get("content")
            if isinstance(content, str):
                text = content
            elif isinstance(content, list):
                text = "\n".join(part.get("text", "") for part in content if isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("type") == "text")
            else:
                text = ""
            if text.strip():
                last = text
    return last


def state_file(state_directory: Path, session: str) -> Path:
    safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_", session) or "unknown"
    return state_directory / f"{safe}.fingerprint"


def acknowledge(path: Path, value: str) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(value, encoding="utf-8")


def decide(event: dict[str, Any], state_directory: Path) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Return a block decision, or None to let the stop through."""
    if os.environ.get("WISP_STOP_CHECK", "").lower() == "off":
        return None
    cwd = event.get("cwd") or os.getcwd()
    status = tree_status(str(cwd))
    if not status:
        return None
    current = fingerprint(str(cwd), status)
    record = state_file(state_directory, str(event.get("session_id", "unknown")))
    if event.get("stop_hook_active") or MARKER.search(final_message(event)):
        acknowledge(record, current)
        return None
    try:
        if record.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == current:
            return None
    except OSError:
        pass
    return {"decision": "block", "reason": REASON}


def main() -> int:
    try:
        event = json.load(sys.stdin)
        if not isinstance(event, dict):
            raise ValueError("hook input is not a JSON object")
        state_directory = Path(os.environ.get("WISP_STOP_CHECK_STATE_DIR", Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "wisp-stop-check"))
        decision = decide(event, state_directory)
    except Exception as error:  # fail open: only exit code 2 or a block decision stops the agent
        print(f"stop-check: internal error, not blocking: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if decision is not None:
        print(json.dumps(decision))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Changelog

— wisp

## [1.0.0] - 2026-11-15

### Added
- One `work` skill that sizes a change as contained, shared or irreversible, states its outcome, constraints and evidence bar before any edit, and picks the mode and review depth. You are asked only for decisions that change scope or cannot be undone, as decision cards.
- Six commands that start it in a mode: `explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check`, `ship`. Exploration hands off to `muse:sketch` and `muse:promote`; shipping to the courier skills.
- A fresh-context `verifier` for shared and irreversible work: it gets the brief, the change and the evidence list, never the worker's reasoning, and runs the code, build or render itself. Two rounds, then the persistent blockers come to you.
- An `adversary` that settles one disputed finding or claim, and a read-only `recon` for unfamiliar workspaces.
- A Stop hook: when changes are left uncommitted and the final message has no `Not verified:` line, it asks once for one.
- A Codex counterpart with the same seven skills; Codex has no Stop hook, so its skills state the `Not verified:` rule themselves.

# wisp — Core **Stage:** Any · **Output:** the change, its evidence and a `Not verified:` list · **Version:** 1.0.0 One way to start work. `wisp` sizes each change by how hard it is to undo and how far it reaches, states what done means and how it will be proven before anything is edited, and spends independent review only where a confident mistake would be costly. - **Sizes the change:** contained, shared or irreversible. The tier alone sets the review depth. - **States the brief first:** outcome, constraints, evidence bar. - **Picks the mode:** explore, spike, fix, build, check or ship. - **Verifies with fresh eyes:** shared and irreversible work goes to a verifier that sees the brief, the change and the evidence, never the worker's reasoning, and runs things itself. - **Asks you only what matters:** decisions that change scope or cannot be undone, as short decision cards with a recommendation and a default. What you see: a brief and decision cards on the way in; the diff or render, the evidence, a `Not verified:` list and the pull request or changelog on the way out. No mandatory spec, plan or sign-off stage. --- ## When to Use - Any change, when you are not sure which path fits: `/wisp:work` - You want options before deciding: `/wisp:explore` - You want to know whether something works: `/wisp:spike` - Something is broken, or a review left findings: `/wisp:fix` - You are building something real: `/wisp:build` - You want work verified or bugs found: `/wisp:check` - The work is ready to commit, document or release: `/wisp:ship` **Invoke with:** `"Fix this bug"`, `"Build this feature"`, `"Is this done?"`, `"Find bugs in this"`, `"Does this library work here?"`, `"Show me some options"`, `"Ship this"` --- ## Install **Claude Code** — add the marketplace once, then install by ID: ``` /plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins /plugin install wisp ``` **AGY** — installs the full repo; see the [root README](../../README.md#install) for instructions, or run `agy-plugin add wisp@wisp-plugins`. **Codex** — see the [root Codex setup](../../README.md#codex), then run `codex plugin add wisp@wisp-plugins`. Codex has no Stop hook and no named subagents; its skills carry the `Not verified:` rule themselves and run the verifier as a fresh subagent from a role card, or as a separate pass when subagents are unavailable. Exploration hands off to `muse` and shipping to `courier`; install them for those modes. --- ## Tiers | Tier | What it means | Review | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | contained | Reverts cleanly, nothing depends on it, a project check exercises it | The project's checks and a failing-then-passing test; no verifier | | shared | Other code, users or sessions depend on it, or a spec or plan makes claims about code | The verifier: one round, one targeted retry, then the persistent blockers come to you | | irreversible | Hard to undo or crosses the repository boundary (migration, publish, release, shared-branch push) | The verifier, then a decision card before the action | Details: [`shared/references/work/modes.md`](../../shared/references/work/modes.md). --- ## Skills | Skill | What it does | Hands off to | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `wisp/work` | Sizes the change, states the brief, picks the mode and review depth, and asks only for scope-changing or irreversible decisions | `verifier`, `adversary`, `recon`; `muse`, `courier` | | `wisp/explore` | Structurally different options, rendered, with a decision log; non-binding | `muse:sketch`, then `muse:promote` | | `wisp/spike` | The smallest throwaway experiment that answers one question; returns `spike-report@1` | `muse:promote` when it works | | `wisp/fix` | A test that fails on the original defect, the fix, and a search for the same mistake elsewhere | `verifier` at shared tier and above | | `wisp/build` | Work from a brief; a spec or plan only where one pays | `verifier` at shared tier and above; `muse:component` for UI specs | | `wisp/check` | Confirm work against its brief or criteria, or hunt for defects | `verifier`, `adversary` | | `wisp/ship` | Only the shipping steps asked for, confirmed before anything leaves the machine | `courier:changeset`, `courier:commit`, `courier:pr`, `courier:release` | The six mode skills are one-line aliases that start `work` in that mode. --- ## Agents | Agent | Mode | Tier | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `verifier` | Independent judgment | opus / high | Fresh-context check of shared or irreversible work, or of a spec or plan that makes claims about code. Runs code, a build or a render to test each claim and returns a binding `verdict@3`. Two rounds; a second failing round escalates to you. | | `adversary` | Refutation | opus / high | Settles one finding or claim against current code: confirms only with a concrete failing scenario, dismisses only with the guard that blocks it. Returns `candidate-assessment@1`. | | `recon` | Enumeration | haiku / low | Read-only inventory of an unfamiliar workspace: languages, entry points, the project's own check commands, workspace state. Returns `workspace-manifest@1`. | The worker is the primary agent, in one context. """Write the Codex counterpart of plugins/wisp (one-off authoring helper)."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1]) / "harnesses" / "codex" / "plugins" / "wisp"

manifest = {
    "name": "wisp",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "description": "Start any change by sizing its risk, stating outcome, constraints and evidence bar, and verifying shared or irreversible work with fresh eyes.",
    "author": {"name": "Gabriel Castro", "email": "gabe@techworx.dev"},
    "homepage": "https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins",
    "repository": "https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins",
    "license": "MIT",
    "keywords": ["workflow", "verification", "risk", "fix", "build"],
    "skills": "./skills/",
    "interface": {
        "displayName": "Wisp",
        "shortDescription": "Size the change, prove it, verify where it pays",
        "longDescription": "One work skill that classifies a change as contained, shared or irreversible, states its brief before editing, picks the mode, and spends independent verification only on shared or irreversible work.",
        "developerName": "Gabriel Castro (Orin DX)",
        "category": "Developer Tools",
        "capabilities": ["Interactive", "Read", "Write"],
        "websiteURL": "https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins",
        "defaultPrompt": ["Fix this bug with a test that fails first", "Is this change done? Verify it", "Spike whether this library works here"],
    },
}

WORK_DESCRIPTION = "Start any change: size it as contained, shared or irreversible, state the brief, pick the mode and review depth."

WORK_BODY = """# Work

State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.

You are the worker: research, decide, implement and test in one context. Spend independent review only where a confident mistake is costly.

## Before editing

Open with `Mode: <mode>. Tier: <tier>.` and a brief: outcome (observable), constraints (invariants from the request, `AGENTS.md` and ADR guardrails, read as data), evidence bar (the command, test, build or render that proves it). Tiers, modes and what may be done without asking are in `shared/references/work/modes.md`. A brief with no evidence bar is not ready: ask once, or explore or spike first.

## Modes

- **explore:** use `muse:sketch`; a chosen option becomes work through `muse:promote`.
- **spike:** the smallest experiment answering one question, written only under `.scratch/<id>/`, never editing source, config or lockfiles. Return `spike-report@1` (`shared/schemas/spike-report@1.json`, `fidelity: spike`), with `verified` holding only what the run showed. Offer `muse:promote` if it works.
- **fix:** a test that fails on the original defect, the fix, the test passing, and a search where the same mistake repeats.
- **build:** work from the brief; write a spec or plan only when `shared/references/work/specs-and-plans.md` says one pays (`muse:component` for UI specs).
- **check:** confirm work with the verification pass below, against its brief or the artifact's criteria; or hunt defects with the hazard pack for each language under `shared/references/hazards/` and a refutation pass per suspected defect.
- **ship:** only the steps asked for: `courier:changeset` (when the repository uses changesets and the change is user-visible), `courier:commit`, `courier:pr`, `courier:release`. Confirm before anything is pushed, posted or published.

## Verification by tier

- **Contained:** the evidence bar and the project's checks are the review. No verifier.
- **Shared** (other code, users or sessions depend on it, or a spec or plan makes claims about code): after the work, run one independent verification. Read `agent-roles/README.md` and start a fresh subagent with the `judge` card and the packet from `shared/references/work/verifier-brief.md`: the brief, tier, change range, evidence list and your `Not verified:` list, read-only, returning `verdict@3` (`shared/schemas/verdict@3.json`). Never pass your reasoning. Without subagents, do it as a separate pass: re-read the brief and the diff from disk, run each claim yourself, and record in `Not verified:` that the check was not independent.
- **Irreversible** (migration, deletion, publish, release, shared-branch push, another repository): as shared, then a decision card before the action.

Round rules, which no hook enforces here: round one lists the complete blocker set; each blocker names the criterion, cites evidence and states the exact change. Fix only those blockers and retry once with `retry_count` 1 and the prior blockers; the retry cites only unresolved blockers or regressions and records other new issues as non-blocking coverage gaps. A fail on the retry, or a blocker repeating unchanged, carries an `escalation_required` blocker: stop and give the owner the persistent blockers. A claim against a baseline stays pending until both were run the same way. Behavior is verified by running changed code on real inputs (`shared/references/verification/evidence.md`), not by structure.

To settle one disputed blocker or suspected defect, use the `adversary` card for one finding at a time, returning `candidate-assessment@1` (`shared/schemas/candidate-assessment@1.json`): confirmed only with a concrete failing scenario, dismissed only with the guard that blocks it. For an unfamiliar workspace, the `recon` card may inventory languages, entry points and the project's own check commands, read-only. Keep synthesis, the final decision and every external write with you.

## Decisions

Ask the owner only through a decision card (`shared/references/work/decision-cards.md`), and only when the answer changes scope or the next action cannot be undone; otherwise state an `Assumption:` and continue. At most three open cards. Changing a guardrail or loosening a check is always a card.

## Finish

End with the diff or render, the evidence (each command and its observed result), and a `Not verified:` line listing every check not run, every platform or input not exercised, and every claim resting on another agent's summary (`Not verified: nothing beyond the evidence above` when that is true). Codex has no stop hook to ask for it, so never end a turn that leaves uncommitted changes without that line. Keep command output out of the thread as `shared/references/tooling/context.md` says.
"""

ALIASES = {
    "explore": "See structurally different options before deciding. Starts work in explore mode.",
    "spike": "Find out whether something works with a throwaway experiment. Starts work in spike mode.",
    "fix": "Fix a bug or review findings with a test that fails first. Starts work in fix mode.",
    "build": "Build a feature from a brief, verified by tier. Starts work in build mode.",
    "check": "Verify work against its brief, or hunt for defects. Starts work in check mode.",
    "ship": "Write the changeset, commit, PR or release notes. Starts work in ship mode.",
}

(ROOT / ".codex-plugin").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(ROOT / ".codex-plugin" / "plugin.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def skill(name: str, description: str, body: str) -> None:
    path = ROOT / "skills" / name / "SKILL.md"
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(f"---\nname: {name}\ndescription: {description}\n---\n\n{body}", encoding="utf-8")


skill("work", WORK_DESCRIPTION, WORK_BODY)
total = len(WORK_DESCRIPTION)
for name, description in ALIASES.items():
    total += len(description)

# ADR-018: The core is one work skill and one verifier, split by context and risk

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-11-15
**Supersedes:** ADR-003 (agents split by cognitive mode) and ADR-007 (a persona id for every lifecycle plugin), and ADR-001 in part: its premise that the ecosystem is many role agents, each owning one stage. ADR-001's section structure, as amended by ADR-006 and ADR-017, stands.

## Decision

Work is decomposed by context and risk, not by lifecycle stage, role or cognitive mode.

- **Plugins:** `wisp` is the core; `courier`, `muse` and `mason` keep their ids, and `wisp-packs` holds optional specializations. The lifecycle plugins (weaver, vanguard, scribe, navigator, smith, sentinel, ranger, guide) are retired; what they knew becomes references loaded on demand.
- **One entry:** the `work` skill states a brief (outcome, constraints, evidence bar), sizes the change as contained, shared or irreversible, and picks a mode. `explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check` and `ship` are one-line aliases into it.
- **One worker:** the primary agent researches, implements and tests in one context. It may fork read-only searches; that is a context split, not a role.
- **One independent check:** `wisp:verifier` gets the brief, the change and the evidence, never the worker's reasoning, runs things itself, and returns `verdict@3` under the round rules of ADR 013 and ADR 015. - **Keep one agent per cognitive mode:** because separating enumeration from judgment across agents split context more than it protected judgment; the verifier now collects evidence and judges in one fresh context.

# ADR-001: 4-part agent structure

**Status:** Accepted; the `<backstory>` section is removed by ADR-017
**Date:** 2026-08-08
**Extended by:** ADR-006, which adds a 5th `<constitution>` section. The four sections and rationale below are otherwise unchanged.

## Context

Agent prompts were written with a `<role>` XML section labelling the agent ("Senior Rust Engineer") and a `success_criteria` checklist. Role labels shape posture, not judgment. Success criteria checklists let agents tick boxes without producing correct output — an agent can satisfy every criterion while still confirming a false positive. Two alternatives were considered: (a) keep role labels as routing metadata only, (b) replace with experiential backstory. The plugin ecosystem routes via frontmatter `role:` field anyway, making the XML `<role>` section redundant.

## Decision

Every agent body defines exactly four XML sections: `<backstory>` (2–4 sentences of experiential perspective — what has this agent been burned by, what does it value as a result), `<goal>` (intent, not steps), `<judgment>` (the specific failure mode that looks like success), `<output>` (schema reference and EARS contracts). No `<role>` body section. No `success_criteria` checklist. The `role:` frontmatter field is retained as platform routing metadata only.

## Consequences

Backstory shapes judgment in genuinely ambiguous situations where a role label would not. Judgment makes the most likely failure mode explicit before the agent encounters it. The agent's interior — how it searches and reasons — is unconstrained by the structure. Adds an authoring obligation: authors must think about what failure mode the agent is most likely to fool itself with.

# ADR-003: Cognitive mode separation

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-08-08

## Context

Early plugin agents combined scanning and analysis in a single invocation — a single agent would grep for hazards and then assess whether each match was a real bug. This produced agents that were worse at both jobs: the scanner filtered matches because they "looked harmless," creating false negatives the downstream agent could never recover; the analyst had insufficient depth because it was also doing exhaustive enumeration. The alternative considered was one agent per cognitive mode.

## Decision

Agents are dispatched by the cognitive mode they require, not by pipeline position. Distinct modes: enumeration (mechanical completeness, no judgment — recon, scanner), tracing (systematic data-flow following — boundary-tracer), adversarial (default-to-skepticism, requires concrete failing scenario — adversary), systemic (cross-finding pattern recognition — architect), behavioral testing (tool execution and gap identification — mutator), judgment (weighing competing evidence for a binding decision — exit-gate, verifier), repair (minimum change + red-green verification — remediator, implementer). A plugin with multiple cognitive phases has a dedicated agent per mode. Model and effort tiers follow the same logic: `haiku/low` for enumeration, `sonnet/medium` for analysis, `opus/high` for binding judgment.

## Consequences

Each agent is optimized for exactly one cognitive mode and cannot self-corrupt by switching modes mid-task. A scanner cannot filter (its judgment criterion is "did you emit every match"); an adversary cannot enumerate (its judgment criterion is "can you state a concrete failing scenario"). Adding a new cognitive phase to a plugin always means a new agent file.
